newsitem.title: ROMANIA: World Bank team to visit Romania to assess reforms.
newsitem.headline: World Bank team to visit Romania to assess reforms.

text.p: A World Bank mission will visit Romania this month to assess the implementation of a financial and enterprise sector adjustment loan (FESAL) project in the country, the Bank said on Tuesday.
"A FESAL supervising mission will visit Romania between October 1 to 10," the Bank's resident mission in Bucharest said in a statement. It gave no other details.

Romania expects a second tranche of FESAL worth $80 million in the fourth quarter of 1996. It got the first $60 million tranche of the $280 million loan, along with a floating tranche of $40 million, in February.
Faster privatisation, including banks sell-off, industrial restructuring and improved financial discipline are key terms under the FESAL accord.

Romania has managed to stabilise its economy and introduced some structural changes but it has been slow to revamp its oversized industries. A bank privatisation bill has yet to be passed by parliament.

The International Monetary Fund, which suspended loans to Bucharest earlier this year on discontent with the local foreign exchange market, recently warned Romania that its failure to carry out structural changes was a threat to economic recovery. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
